newsitem.title: USA: U.S. accuses Serbia of tying polls in legal knots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. accuses Serbia of tying polls in legal knots.

text.p: The United States said on Tuesday it was "extremely disturbed" by the Serbian government's handling of the country's local election dispute and accused Belgrade of tying up the issue in legal knots.
The U.S. State Department also condemned Serbian authorities for resorting to violence against opposition protesters.

The statement came after Yugoslav courts on Monday dealt new blows to the Zajedno opposition group, suspending a previous election commission finding that Zajedno had won Belgrade and awarding the ruling Socialists victory in another town, Sabac.
Zajedno, backed by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), says it captured Belgrade, Sabac and 12 other cities in the Nov. 17 poll.
"The United States continues to be extremely disturbed by the actions of the Serbian government," said State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns.
"They are now tying up this question of respect for elections in a judicial process that cannot be considered to be democratic by any means," he told a news briefing.

Burns said Washington had been hopeful last week that the Serbian government, faced with nine weeks of opposition demonstrations, would back down and let Zajedno take its seats in the Belgrade city assembly and elsewhere.

But now, he said, Serbian authorities had "tied this up in judicial knots. And they've begun to use force -- physical force -- against demonstrators in the streets of Belgrade. This is not a positive turn in these developments."

Burns warned Belgrade that "the international community will not react positively in any way to the use of violence and the threat of the use of violence against protesters who have been exercising their rights peacefully".
"We condemn the use of force against protesters in the streets of Belgrade," the U.S. spokesman said.

Washington and its allies continued to insist that the OSCE recommendations be respected, that the Nov. 17 election results should stand and that the opposition should be able to take its seats in city councils, he said.
